intro: Pick the best one. Hints are here if you want them.

items.stem: Which one is outside information that does work on Document 10?

options.1: In 1829 the Stephensons' Rocket won the Rainhill Trials, which shows steam was ready to pull the trains
options.2: In 1830 the railway ran about 30 miles between the port of Liverpool and the mill town of Manchester
options.3: Liverpool and Manchester are both cities in the northwest of England, not very far from the sea
options.4: Railways are still used in Britain today to carry people and goods between its largest cities

hints: One of these is already inside Document 10. Cross it off first.
Of the rest, which one proves something about the railway instead of just sitting there?
items.reason: Option 2 is in the document, so it can't be outside information. Options 3 and 4 are true but they only sit there. The Rainhill Trials are outside the document and show the railway had an engine ready to run it.

items.stem: Which one is outside information that does work on Document 8?

options.1: Ure wrote that steam engines put multitudes of miners, engineers, ship-builders and sailors to work, and caused canals to be built
options.2: Andrew Ure was a writer who studied factories, and his book was all about the factory system
options.3: In 1785 a steam engine first drove a cotton mill's machines directly, which shows steam had reached the mills
options.4: Steam engines are machines that use the power of steam from boiling water to make things move

hints: One of these is a quotation from Document 8.
Which one names something that happened, with a date, and proves Ure's point?
items.reason: Option 1 is the document. Option 2 comes from the source line. Option 4 is a definition that does no work. Papplewick, 1785, is outside the document and shows steam powering mill machines, which backs up Ure.

items.stem: Which one is outside information that does work on Document 2?

options.1: Young wrote that by nineteen enclosure bills in twenty the poor were injured, some grossly injured
options.2: Parliament passed thousands of enclosure acts, which shows the harm Young admitted reached families across the country
options.3: Arthur Young was a well-known writer on farming, and he supported the enclosure of the open fields
options.4: Farming has changed a great deal since 1801, and most British people today live in towns

hints: Two of these are already in Document 2, its words or its introduction.
Which fact makes Young's admission bigger?
items.reason: Options 1 and 3 are inside the document: its quotation and its introduction. Option 4 sits there. Thousands of enclosure acts, from What You Need to Know, shows the injury Young admitted was not a few villages but the whole country.
